title: Show OSD feedback when audio output is disabled via Icons-Only Task Manager Icon
line: Clicking the speaker badge on a Task Manager icon now shows an "App Muted" OSD, and the app's volume when unmuting.
explanation: Clicking the small speaker badge on a task muted the app's audio streams, and the only feedback was the badge turning into a slashed speaker, so accidental clicks (e.g. while switching windows in a call) went unnoticed. The badge's click and keyboard handlers now also call plasmashell's existing org.kde.osdService mediaPlayerVolumeChanged, which shows "<App> Muted" when muting and the app's volume bar when unmuting, the same OSD media players use.

commits.message:
applets/taskmanager: show an OSD when muting from the audio indicator

Clicking the speaker badge on a task muted the app with only a small
change to the badge as feedback, so accidental clicks went unnoticed.
It now shows the "App Muted" OSD used for players, and volume on unmute.

BUG: 432203

media.caption: Master: clicking the badge mutes ffplay with no OSD, only the tiny slashed badge
Fix: clicking the badge shows "ffplay Muted"
Fix: clicking it again shows the app's volume as it unmutes

reviews.text: Clean, idiomatic fix that calls plasmashell's existing org.kde.osdService.mediaPlayerVolumeChanged when toggling mute from the task audio indicator badge via mouse or keyboard. Reusing the existing OSD avoids new translatable strings, automatically respects the global OSD setting, and keeps deliberate tooltip/context-menu mute actions quiet while giving clear feedback for accidental badge clicks. Screenshots and verification confirm mute and unmute behavior cleanly.
